data.case_title: Suspicious "energy refund" letter demanding an upfront fee
data.title: Suspicious "energy refund" letter demanding an upfront fee
data.summary: An outfit calling itself "Verbraucher-Rückerstattungsstelle Energie", based in Nicosia, Cyprus, claims that Johanna Beispielacker is owed a €612.00 refund from energy bills for 2023–2025. It demands a one-off €49.90 "processing fee" be transferred to a Cypriot account before 27 November 2026, promising payout within 48 hours and threatening the claim will lapse otherwise.
data.explanation: This letter shows strong signs of an advance-fee scam (Vorkasse-Betrug): a supposed refund office with no verifiable German authority status, asking for a fee to be paid to a foreign (Cyprus) account before releasing money it says is already "approved", and pressuring with a tight deadline and total forfeiture if you don't pay. Genuine energy refunds in Germany are never conditional on paying a fee first. Do not transfer any money or share bank details. If in doubt, contact your actual energy provider directly or a consumer protection centre (Verbraucherzentrale) to verify, and consider reporting this letter as a scam.

warnings: This has the hallmarks of an advance-fee scam: it demands an upfront fee before releasing a promised refund, which legitimate German energy-refund processes never require.
The payee IBAN (CY...) is registered in Cyprus, which is highly unusual and a red flag for a claimed German consumer-refund office.
The sender's email domain (rueckerstattung-energie.example) and the generic company name are not linked to any known, verifiable German authority or consumer protection body.
The letter uses urgency and a threat of permanent forfeiture to pressure quick payment, a common manipulation tactic in scams.
